Title: ACL Tears: Female Athletes Are Up To 8 Times More Likely To Get One

Description:
If you play soccer, basketball, or volleyball, you've probably heard of someone tearing their ACL. Female athletes are up to 8 times more likely to tear one than male athletes — at the last two Women's World Cups, 12.5% of players had already had ACL surgery, nearly double the men's rate.

Women's ACLs tend to be smaller with a narrower bony notch, and hip alignment plus hormonal shifts add to the risk. Most tears happen with no contact at all — just a bad landing or sudden pivot.

Protect the knee right away if you suspect a tear (ice, elevate, get it checked within days), and train how you land — structured programs have cut ACL injuries by up to 88% in young female soccer players.
